WHAT_THIS_IS:
Score the pilot's four finished models on the ENTIRE held-out slice.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Every loss number in both pilot write-ups was computed on a
SINGLE 1024-token passage (bursts/context.txt). That passage is held out -- it
is openwebtext document 73, and the held-out slice is taken from the FRONT of
the corpus precisely so the committed texts fall outside training -- so it
carries no memorisation confound. What it does carry is sampling noise: one
passage is one draw, and docs/2026-08-05-training-objective-defect.md measured
sd = 1.007 nats ACROSS held-out windows for a single model.

The study's sample size is set by sigma/delta. Both terms were estimated from
that one passage. This re-estimates both over all 10,240 held-out sequences,
which is what cross-module obligation 1 reserved the slice for and what
docs/measurements/10-metrics.md says to do "once against trained checkpoints".

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. It does not change the study's metric. The barrier and the
section 8.4 branch are untouched; this is the endpoint-loss axis only, measured
on more text. Nothing here is arm-vs-twin-before-the-branch: the branch is
already recorded twice (docs/measurements/12-injection-point-ruler.json), so
section 8.5 constraint 1 is discharged.

THE PAIRING POINT, which is the reason the numbers below matter. The study's
test is a paired difference WITHIN seed (preregistration section 4, and
scripts/analysis.py's paired_differences). Its noise term is the sd ACROSS
SEEDS of that paired difference. The pilot has exactly one seed with an
injecting arm, so it cannot estimate that quantity, and both write-ups
substituted the UNPAIRED sd (twin-vs-twin across seeds, x sqrt(2)) instead.
This script cannot fix that either -- it reports the per-window spread of each
pair so the substitution's size is at least visible.

windows.selection: every held-out sequence in file order

CAVEAT_ON_SIGMA: unpaired_sigma is what BOTH pilot write-ups used. It is NOT the noise term of the study's test, which is the sd ACROSS SEEDS of the within-seed paired difference. One injecting arm at one seed cannot estimate that. See the module docstring.
